title: The graph transformation into the Hilbert functor is an open immersion
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $Z\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $X\to S$ be separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Write $Z_T=Z\times_ST$, $X_T=X\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The graph construction is a natural injective transformation from $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_T(Z_T,X_T)$ into the functor of closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] of $(Z\times_SX)_T$ that are proper, flat and finitely presented over $T$. This transformation is representable by open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]. Explicitly, for each such closed subscheme $D\subset Z_T\times_TX_T$, there is an open $U\subset T$ such that, for every $T'\to T$, $D_{T'}\to Z_{T'}$ is an isomorphism exactly when $T'\to T$ factors through $U$. On this open the corresponding morphism is $\operatorname{pr}_2\circ(\operatorname{pr}_1|_D)^{-1}$. In particular, any representing Hilbert scheme contains the relative morphism functor as this open subscheme, with universal evaluation and compatibility with all base changes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-hilbert-graph-family-base-change] to the given $Z\to S$ and $X\to S$. It constructs the actual closed graph families and the natural transformation $\gamma$ into the stated proper Hilbert presheaf, and gives properness, flatness and finite presentation of every $Z_T\to T$.

For a Hilbert family $D$ over $T$, let $k:D\to Z_T$ be the first projection. Apply [lem-sfb-universal-isomorphism-open] with $B=T$, $A=D$, $C=Z_T$, $p:D\to T$ and $q:Z_T\to T$. The proper Hilbert-family definition [def-sfb-proper-hilbert-presheaf] makes $p$ flat, finitely presented and proper. Thus $p$ is locally of finite presentation and universally closed. Step 1 makes $q$ proper, hence separated, locally of finite type and closed, by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. All six hypotheses hold. The resulting open $U_D\subseteq T$ has the required isomorphism criterion for every test map, without any finiteness or flatness condition on $X/S$.

Use [lem-sfb-graph-projection-functor-comparison] with $F$ the proper Hilbert presheaf and with $\gamma$ from Step 1. Step 2 supplies its universal first-projection opens. The comparison identifies each $h_T\times_F\mathcal M$ with $h_{U_D}$, proves injectivity, and recovers the unique morphism as $\operatorname{pr}_2\circ(\operatorname{pr}_1|_D)^{-1}$. If $H$ represents $F$, the same comparison at its universal family gives the open representing scheme, its evaluation and compatibility with every base change. These are all the remaining conclusions.
